question: Was every line of the 5 GB review file read?
why: Reading in chunks must not drop the end of a chunk or the end of the file.
detail: 6,990,280 lines in the file, 6,990,280 rows read

question: Does any review appear twice?
why: A duplicated review would count one opinion twice.

question: Is every rating a whole number from 1 to 5?
why: Anything else would mean the file was parsed wrongly.

question: Do the review dates fall inside the dataset's time span?
why: The template code parsed dates with ymd(), which fails on timestamps; this confirms the fix.

question: Does every review belong to a restaurant in the theme?
why: A wrong join key would attach reviews to the wrong restaurants or lose them.
detail: 0 reviews without a restaurant, 0 restaurants without reviews

question: Do our review counts agree with the counts in Yelp's business file?
why: An independent number from a different file: if the join lost reviews, these would disagree.
detail: correlation 0.99998; our count is never lower, and is higher by a median of 2 reviews

question: Do our averages agree with the star rating Yelp shows for each restaurant?
why: Yelp rounds its rating to half stars, so the two should differ by 0.25 at most, apart from the few extra reviews above.
detail: 97.5% of restaurants within 0.25 stars, largest difference 0.35

question: Is every restaurant inside the official city boundary?
why: This is the project's definition of a New Orleans restaurant.

question: Does every theme restaurant have a part of town and a neighborhood?
why: A restaurant without an area would silently drop out of the area comparison.
detail: 0 without a part of town, 0 without a neighborhood

question: Do well-known restaurants land in the neighborhoods they are known to be in?
why: A spatial join can be wrong in ways that counts cannot show, for example swapped latitude and longitude.
detail: 8 of 8 landmarks in the expected neighborhood

question: Does the inclusion rule hold for every restaurant?
why: Each theme restaurant must carry one of the four labels, and none of the excluded ones may be inside.
detail: 608 restaurants in the theme, 51 left out by the seafood exception, overlap 0

question: Do restaurant averages computed a second way give the same numbers?
why: The stored averages come from dplyr; this recomputes them with base R.

question: Do each reviewer's adjusted ratings average to zero?
why: By definition a reviewer rates exactly at their own usual level on average; anything else is a bug.

question: Does a stricter reviewer baseline change the adjusted ranking?
why: The simple baseline includes the review being judged. Leaving it out is cleaner in theory; this shows it makes no practical difference.
detail: correlation 0.9995, 10 of the adjusted top 10 in common

question: Are the ranks complete, from 1 to the number of ranked restaurants?
why: Gaps or ties in the ranks would shift the top 10.

question: Does the bootstrap give the same chances with a different random seed?
why: The chance of being in the top 10 should not depend on the random numbers used.
detail: largest change in any restaurant's chance: 0.028

question: Does the top 10 survive a different definition of an active reviewer?
why: The assignment asks how the threshold changes the results.
detail: threshold 3: 9 of 10 remain; threshold 5: 10 of 10 remain; threshold 10: 9 of 10 remain

question: Do the parts of town add up to all ranked restaurants?
why: Every ranked restaurant must be counted in exactly one part of town.
detail: 231 restaurants in 11 parts of town, 58 of them great

question: Does the leading part of town stay first when 'great' is defined differently?
why: The answer should not hinge on the 25% cut-off.
detail: best 10%: place 3; best 20%: place 1; best 25%: place 1; best 33%: place 1
